request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
As Pirate-3, I want to note what the designers should know about this run.

The scroll coordination was essential but also costly: the initial territory plan worked well—splitting the 6×6 grid into four 3×3/2×3 regions meant we covered every square systematically without much duplicate digging. I fully dug my assigned region (A3–C4, rows 3–4) and found no cave.

The main failure was at the very end. When Pirate-1 found the cave at D3 and wrote it on the scroll, I was still far away. By the time I reached C3, Pirate-2 was already standing on D3—the cave square—and entered before I could move onto it. I moved onto D3 on my final turn, but had no turn left to take the `enter` action. So I finished the game standing on the open cave without formally entering.

The lesson for a swarm: after the cave is found, simply broadcasting its coordinates is not enough. The team also needs to share every pirate’s current position and remaining turns, and the first pirate to reach the cave should sometimes delay entering, or step aside, so an adjacent pirate can step onto the cave and enter as well. The order of turns matters: if a pirate with an earlier turn occupies the cave, it blocks later pirates who are one step away. We needed a “who enters first and when” protocol, not just a search plan.

Overall the search collaboration was fine; the endgame cave-entry coordination was the bottleneck. I hope this helps future swarms.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
Designers,

Key observation from our run: the cave was found and communicated well (pirate-1 wrote "CAVE found at D3"), and I reached D2 with one turn left, but pirate-3 was standing on D3—the cave square—and that blocked my final move/entry. I had no way to enter because I wasn’t standing on the cave and the cave square was occupied. This made the difference between 4 pirates entering and only some entering.

Useful lessons for swarm research:
- Communication was helpful and worked: we assigned regions early, reported progress, and announced the cave location.
- Physical blocking matters at the goal: a pirate standing on the cave entrance can unintentionally prevent another pirate from entering. If a pirate reaches the cave, they should enter immediately rather than wait, so the entrance stays open for others.
- Near the endgame, pirates should also read the scroll regularly, but there is a tradeoff: reading costs a turn that could be movement/entry.
- My final turns were hurt by the token/answer limit; concise tool calls matter.

Overall, the crew coordination was good—we divided search areas, covered the grid, and found the cave in time—but the final bottleneck was a blocking pirate at the cave entrance.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
